_header: Parity fixture for llm/retry.rs and llm/credentials.rs -> llm-sidecar/src/llm/{retry,credentials}.ts.

Generated by driving the real Rust classifiers in a throwaway worktree at 9023b46d (the last commit where the daemon crate builds). The generator is not committed; nothing regenerates this file. A later diff against it is a defect, not a fixture to update.

`LlmError` is not serde — it wraps a reqwest::Error — so errors are carried as a `kind` discriminator the replay rebuilds from. LlmError::Request is absent for the same reason: constructing one needs real I/O. Both functions treat it exactly as the other transport errors, which the replay covers directly.

resolve_key_candidates takes a whole ProviderRegistry in Rust. The fixture records the normalized entry that registry produced, because parsing the [providers] TOML belongs to the config module and not to this port.

REMOVED by #16, not lost: the `is_refusal` (25 cases) and `should_retry_refusal` (48 cases) sections, the 56 `should_retry_error` cases whose expected decision was `fallback_model`, the 8 whose error was `refusal`, and the 1 `classify_credential_failure` case for that error. Refusal detection and model fallback were deleted from both languages — no production caller ever set a fallback model or constructed the refusal error. What remains (336 retry decisions, 24 classifications, and every other section) is still the frozen 9023b46d recording and is still untouched. The `policy.fallback_model` field survives in the remaining records because they are recordings; it no longer exists in either implementation and the replay ignores it.

resolve_key_candidates.name: no providers section entry at all
explicitly disabled provider resolves to nothing
disabled keys are filtered, order of the rest preserved
every key disabled falls through to the legacy single key
enabled provider declaring no keys keeps the static env working
unknown provider with no model env gets the LLM_API_KEY default
a disabled provider stays empty even with a model env set
